summary: Added `using System.Diagnostics;` to the top of DiffService.cs (was not previously imported).

Step 1 (LCS loop): Added Debug.Assert for both reference[ri].LineNumber.HasValue and current[ci].LineNumber.HasValue before the existing ?? (ri+1)/(ci+1) fallbacks. Added a comment explaining the invariant (FileService.ReadFileAsync always sets LineNumber) and why the proxy-position fallback is kept as defensive code.

Step 3 (remainingNew loop): Added Debug.Assert for m.LineNumber.HasValue before the existing ?? 0 sentinel fallback. Added a comment explaining the invariant and explicitly noting why the 0 sentinel differs from the Step 1 proxy (0 is outside the valid line-number range so unpositioned entries are naturally excluded from replacement matching).

Step 6 (shiftedLines): Removed the vacuous .Where(s => s.ReferenceNumber.HasValue) LINQ filter and replaced it with Debug.Assert(shiftedLines.All(s => s.ReferenceNumber.HasValue), ...) with an explanatory message. The .OrderBy call now operates directly on shiftedLines without the preceding filter.

Tests: 439 pass, 1 pre-existing locale-dependent failure in ProfileServiceTests.GenerateProfileId_AccentedCharacters_RemovesAccents — unrelated to DiffService and pre-dates this WP.

Edge-case analysis: (1) Debug.Assert is a no-op in Release — fallbacks remain as intended by WP rationale. (2) shiftedLines.All(...) in the Step 6 assert is O(n) but Debug-only — zero cost in Release. (3) Empty lcs path is safe (Step 1 body skips, Step 6 skipped via Count guard). (4) If Step 1 assert fires (Debug), execution continues with proxy refPos; Step 6 assert remains consistent because DiffLineModel.ReferenceNumber is non-null int? constructed from int refPos.

comments.note: Debug.Assert is elided in Release builds — if LineNumber were ever null in a Release scenario, the ?? fallbacks would silently activate with no diagnostic signal. This is the explicitly accepted trade-off per the WP rationale (fallbacks kept as defensive code). No action required.

shiftedLines.All(s => s.ReferenceNumber.HasValue) in the Step 6 Debug.Assert is O(n) over the shifted-lines list. In Release the assert is elided; in Debug for typical load-order sizes this is negligible. No action required.
